research_rationale: EO 6539-A (December 27, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text has an introductory 'Whereas' paragraph (the Secretary of Agriculture's submission, report, recommendations and findings), a findings paragraph with five numbered findings (application, notice and hearings, compliance with section 3(a) clauses (1) and (2), and tendency to effectuate the policy of section 1), and one operative paragraph ending 'do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry.' The machine inventory lists the five numbered findings as five clauses (the fifth span also swallows the operative paragraph and the signature line); findings command nothing, so I replaced it with one clause, characters 1402 to 1676, the operative approval sentence (inventory correction recorded). Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6539-approval-code-fair-competition-for-the-wine-industry.txt, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; 1,738 characters). APP page check (AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, working-text paragraph): the jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with sha256 869906b7aeaa2827a73b7c337d75455e2e66975ed00a8799f2c14b4007564f81 is headed 'Executive Order 6539-A—Approval of Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry', dated December 27, 1933, node app:node/373337, Common Crawl capture 2025-10-15T14:33:52Z; its text_sha256 a3e6e48e95fff804f05f47bd23bec0b2f97ddbf64c1d468fbcf0c1a2a7f08a00 equals the sha256 I computed for the held file, and the page heading (which names the number), the date and the subject agree with the text. Cotton holds the exact page bytes (jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output/captures). Identity also agrees with the census register row and the WPA 1944 list (page 560: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry ap proved.'). Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2.
savings_reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.

research_rationale: EO 6549-A (January 4, 1934) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wholesale Food and Grocery Trade to become effective in place of the earlier Code of Labor Provisions approved November 15, 1933, subject to six conditions. Conditions (1) and (2) provide that Section 13 and paragraph 4 of Section 12 of Article VII shall not be effective until 30 days after the date the code becomes effective; neither the order nor any held source states the date the code became effective, so the own-terms end of those deferrals cannot be computed. Conditions (3) and (4) direct the Administrator to consider the right of a wholesale grocers association to representation on the code authority and to call a hearing as soon as practicable; these are directions to an officer with no held record of performance or end. Condition (6) gives the Administrator power to disapprove acts of the code authority. Each needs its own end; the approval and condition (5) alone would be a plain repeal case.

research_rationale: EO 6723 (May 26, 1934) suspends 'until further orders' the provisions of codes of service trades or industries that the Administrator later designates (except child labor, maximum hours, minimum pay and sections 7(a) and 10(b)), lets members display NRA insignia only while complying with the unsuspended provisions, authorizes the Administrator to make an agreement with the President, on 85 percent proposals, to abide by a local code of fair trade practices, and lets the Administrator supplement the order. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet).
